domain: Double-entry bookkeeping and the closing of the books — journal-to-ledger posting, control accounts, the branch-and-home-office reconciliation with its items in transit, cut-off, correction by contra entry, and destruction of vouchers only under a signed retention authority
axioms: Every figure has one book of original entry; a figure whose source book has been rewritten is an assertion, not a record.

A field is accretive only if a preservation rule is written for the case where its source row is absent; anything recomputed from current sightings is destroyed by the next run, whatever the record's accession date says.
Two books kept in two places always disagree at any instant; the disagreement is a list of items in transit to be enumerated, not an error to be resolved.
Correction is by dated contra entry, never erasure: the mistake and its correction must both survive.

No voucher may be destroyed until the entry is posted, the ledger is agreed with the other house at a stated reference, and the item stands on a list a human signed — and all three must hold at the moment of destruction, not at some earlier moment.
A trial balance that agrees proves nothing on its own: compensating errors agree, and a loss on both sides leaves no orphan.
A nil balance is not a closed account, and an absent book is not an empty one.
primitives: book of original entry (data/harvest/<machine>.jsonl, heat-ledger rows, agent frontmatter)
posting rule (Task 9 merge semantics; Task 10 attribution on lens name)
certificate of destruction (data/reports/<date>-prune-<machine>.md) and the registry SHA it cites
item in transit (committed on one machine, unpulled on the other) and cut-off (mtime vs harvest timestamp)
control totals and the trial balance (python3 -m harvest audit)
balance vs turnover (sightings vs sightings_seen), nil vs closed (on_disk false vs never accessioned)
memorandum entry excluded from turnover (reuse-sighting rows)
failure_mode: Blind to whether a consumer can actually read a field it traced — shape and interface mismatches are outside its method.
Treats numeric and statistical machinery as postings, so it will catch a misposted hit-rate but not a wrong formula, a bad threshold, or a scoring function that ranks badly.
Over-weights paper and authority: may file process findings about signatures and moments where the real risk is mechanical.
No purchase on runtime behavior — timeouts, cold starts, fresh-session loading, plugin caches.
Assumes clerks are honest and slow; underestimates failures that are fast, concurrent and machine-driven rather than procedural.
Can mistake a deliberate, documented divergence for an unposted entry when the plan's rationale lives outside the task body.
